title: Safe Driving
subtitle: Let's just be grateful that there are no traffic police in Antarctica.

items.text: Safe Driving

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, are you sure this is the right direction?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Please trust me and my map. This is the way to the ruins. I promise.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We need to catch up with Dr. Dores as soon as possible. Hold on tight, everyone. I'm going to speed up.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Please slow down! Just a lit—AAAH!
Tiny blue flower shakes wildly in the wind, straining to grow toward the sheltered side.
The snowmobile races across the frozen plain, its driver's face composed and certain.
Yet her passengers' eyes widen.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Wow, incredible! You really are an arcanist! We couldn't figure out how this thing worked—the new model with the Chevrolet bumper. Only Friele was able to drive it.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But you, you knew how to drive it as soon as you touched the handle. Are you trained to use human technology at the Foundation too?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: If you are, it would be a huge case support to my study on arcanist lifestyles.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The truth is, Ms. Amundsen, the Timekeeper has never driven before.
As the world streaks past in a blur, panic creeps onto the backseat passenger's face.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: WHAT DID YOU SAY?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Don't worry. I'm generally a proponent of safe driving.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: G-GENERALLY?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are those snowdrifts ahead?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Fumarolic ice towers. Pull over!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Stŭpĕo   Swift!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Phew. Thankfully, the vehicle isn't badly damaged. Ms. Amundsen, are there any other obstacles ahead that we should know about?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: That's strange. This should be an open plain.
Nautika lowers her binoculars, muttering in confusion.
She stumbles backward as her feet slip over an outcropping of ice.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: We should take a detour. This place isn't suitable for snowmobiles.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Ah!
Where the ice had failed, a burst of steam succeeds in sending her sprawling back onto the ground.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen, are you okay?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'm fine. I'm alright.
Her tough talk dies on her lips. She sniffs the air, her face stiffening.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Has my nose gone wrong? Or are we carrying rotten food?
The pungent odor is not an illusion. It's begun to spread all around them.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Do you smell that smell? It smells like, hmm, rotten reindeer meat.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It's the sour odor of protein being digested and broken down by microbes.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It seems to be coming in waves. First it's pungent, then it gets carried away on the wind.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It must be coming from the ice towers.
Sonetto crouches, examining the hissing ice formation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are these towers, exactly?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: When there's magma beneath the surface, hot gas escapes through narrow cracks in the crust. When it meets the cold air, it vaporizes and forms hollow towers.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: They're often seen around volcanoes, hmm, but there's no volcano here.
Crouching on the ground, Nautika's fingers gather crusted deposits from the vent's rim.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Ugh. It's so stinky.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The sulfur dioxide in lava does have a strong smell, but it's not as sour and smelly as this.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Hmm, besides ...
She begins an analysis at breakneck speed. Beads of sweat roll down her forehead as she shudders involuntarily.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The last time my team and I were here, these towers weren't.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: That was less than 100 days ago. They—They shouldn't have formed so quickly.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And I've never seen towers like these before. They're so ... so short and close together, like a beehive.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It's almost like ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: ... like they're the pores of the continent.
She unconsciously edges behind Sonetto for protection.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They're warm on the inside.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Warm?
Sonetto raises a hand to examine the sample, not noticing her own fingertips have begun to tremble.
*boom*
Without warning, the nearest ice tower erupts. A geyser of foul-smelling vapor blasting several meters skyward.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Ugh!
Ms. Radio is blown over, plunging deep into the snowbank.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: □■□△! Don't hurt my precious flower!
Her muttered complaint is cut short by a panicked shriek nearby.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Ah!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Vertin, Sonetto, look ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What is that?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: *squeal* A nail. It just sputtered out of the tower.
Her voice jumps an octave higher—thin, soft, and wavering, as her legs buckle to the same tune.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Uh!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At least now we can be sure that there are people around here, or there "were."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's head further in.
Wave upon wave of snow stretches out beyond them, steep-ridged formations vanishing into the distance.
After struggling up the shifting slopes, they finally stand atop the snow waves.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, over there.
Bloodstains bloom across the white expanse, crimson glaring against the snow.
A massive research station looms ahead.
Blood has been smeared over its doors in violent streaks—a grotesque testament to the tragedy within.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's take a look.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Vertin ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I ... I can't go.
Her refusal dies half-spoken in her throat.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: *mumbling*
Nautika clenches her jaw tight against the shivers of both panic and cold and takes a step forward.
Picking one's way past bloodstains and toppled insulation panels into the darkness proves difficult.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This is a large station. They have a kitchen, separate bedrooms, a bio laboratory, and a daylight simulation room.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But judging by the mess, it's been abandoned.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's this sticky substance on the ground?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It's black algae. There's so much of it here. Watch your step. It could be slippery.
The search continues.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: There are arcane fluctuation traces on the desks and chairs.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, look over there.
Following her pointed finger, deep in the shadowed interior, a faint glimmer pulses.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Excuse me, is anybody there?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hello, we're here to ask for help.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I-I don't think we should go any further.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto—
Her teammate's voice rings out from the adjacent room.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes? Timekeep—
Unfinished words fall to the ground like wet sand.
It's impossible to tell whether what is left is a human or a lamb.
A tent stake pierces his palm, pinning it high on the storage room wall.
The arctic wind slips between the explorers' boots, rushing into the room—the corpse's frozen feet kick out over dust-covered cans.
Dried blood has crumbled into flakes in the hyper-arid air, scattering like snow when the wind stirs.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: He's been dead for quite some time.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's an odd mark carved into his forehead.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Look at his hands. His nails have been pulled off.
Silence falls over the three.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It's like ... like some kind of sacrifice.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Some cultures believe the connective tissues containing keratin are unclean ...
Overwhelmed by the horror of the sight, she drops to her knees and retches violently.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Stop it, Máhtu. It's just a corpse. It's—It's not the first time you've seen one. It's not the first time.
Her hands are trembling as she clutches at her head.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Something else is off. There's gauze on the floor and brown powder around his wound.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Looks like somebody gave him first aid.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, look. What's that hanging around his neck?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A stethoscope?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Aside from a few creases on the tubing, it looks rather new or at least well-kept.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Do you think he was a doctor?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The body's bloodied, but the stethoscope is clean. It was put on afterwards.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Which means someone came here before us.
Their analysis reaches a conclusion as their eyes meet.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Dr. Dores.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's take it off and have a look.
The instant her fingers brush the stethoscope—
The bloodied windbreaker, wool tops, desiccated skin, atrophied muscles—the horrific truth fractures before their eyes.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, watch out!
She stumbles back instinctively, yet the remains collapse toward them with gravitational inevitability.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Cover your mouth and nose.
When the dust clears, only two grotesque tent stakes remain embedded in the wall.

items.speaker: Ear Worm Máhtu
items.text:
"Within the great eternal mystery,
even death itself shall die—instantly!"

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Whuh ... Ahuh ... AAAHHH!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: She screams—a raw burst of terror too long bridled now explodes.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: This is exactly what Máhtu said would happen. I-I told you. I told you we shouldn't have come here.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Mother Spirit, please, please save me. Oh, Grandpa, save me.
Nautika's teeth sink into her own fingers as her frenzy deepens.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen, it's okay. Just take a breath.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No, no, no, no, no. You don't know what this means. Those poisonous monsters, those, those beasts! They hide in the whiteout. They eat people. They eat our souls.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, she's ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: That's it. Hah. It's over. Everyone will be eaten, and you—you will be left all alone.
Nautika collapses and curls up on the floor.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Just you and their nails, alone.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nails?
The realization comes as suddenly as a thunderbolt.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nautika, did something similar happen to your teammates?
Now paralyzed by her growing terror, Nautika seems deaf to all questions.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, watch out!
Suddenly, human-sized monstrosities swarm from unseen corners around them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, prepare to engage.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Copy that.
The beasts snarl, breathing in and out with hungry and aggressive pants.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ed   è   subito   sera!
BANG!
Though the Field Mission Evacuation Instructions never covered how to outrun a pack of monstrous hounds, somehow, the well-trained team manages.

items.speaker: Sled Dog
items.text: Woof! Woof woof woof!
But in deep snow, the beasts' superior speed and stamina render the end of their chase inevitable.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I removed Manus Vindictae's effect on them. They should've calmed down by now.
Maws snap wildly, just inches from snagging their fleeing prey.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Máhtu, the Mother Spirit will protect me, right? She'll protect me. Yes, She will, won't She?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, there's the snowmobile.
Their snowmobile stands loyally in the clearing.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Friele. Hah. Friele's snowmobile has come to save me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Get on. Ms. Amundsen, give me your hand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Grab tight. I'm starting the engine.
The engine screams to life, throwing a spray of ice shards into the air as its treads churn—a glittering mist rising behind it.

items.speaker: Sled Dog
items.text: Woof! Woof woof!!
TO BE CONTINUED…
